new_symbol_range_suggestions.infectious_saturation: positive; typically comparable to moderate infectious fractions where source-side overlap begins to reduce marginal transmission, e.g. from well below 1 up to several times the observed I range

derivation_notes: The parent assumed first-order transmission in infectious prevalence. Here that source-side law is refined so overlapping contact neighborhoods or repeated competition for the same susceptible contacts make total transmission increase sublinearly with I through the saturating factor I/(infectious_saturation + I).
change_summary: Changed the transmission law from exactly linear in infectious prevalence to a finite-capacity source-side saturation. This directly bends the scored mapping dI_dt(S,I,B) downward at moderate I while preserving the parent approximately when infectious prevalence stays small relative to infectious_saturation.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Transmission is first-order in the infectious fraction, with no saturation or overlap on the infectious source side.
assumption_audit.mechanism: At moderate prevalence, infectious individuals increasingly share overlapping susceptible contact opportunities, so additional infectious individuals are less than proportionally productive.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Taking infectious_saturation to infinity recovers the parent transmission law.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed S and removal terms, the transmission contribution to dI_dt is proportional to I times a burden-suppressed saturating function of S, so the net per-capita growth changes approximately linearly with I near low prevalence aside from the lagged burden effect.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the implicit first-order infectiousness assumption with a saturating contribution of infectious burden to transmission, so at fixed S and removal terms the transmission contribution grows sublinearly with I when I is not small, bending the dI_dt-versus-I relation downward even before removal dominates.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories that reach moderate infectious prevalence while S is still appreciable, the rise of I slows earlier and the epidemic peak is broader/lower than the parent predicts; near very small I the child remains close to the parent.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when I reaches a non-negligible fraction of the population while S remains above the contact-limitation scale, so repeated contacts, local overlap, or finite effective mixing make added infectious individuals less than proportionally productive; weak when I stays very small throughout.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early-to-mid epidemic growth already shows slight downward bending of dI_dt versus I at moderate prevalence; in holdout, larger peaks extend this same mechanism into clearer sublinear transmission and stronger peak flattening without changing the sign structure.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the infectious-saturation scale to infinity, which restores exactly first-order transmission in I.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: source-side saturation of infectious contribution to transmission
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: At moderate prevalence, infectious individuals increasingly compete for the same susceptible contacts or share overlapping contact neighborhoods, so total force of infection rises sublinearly with infectious abundance even in a closed homogeneous benchmark.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of the target mapping with respect to I: the marginal transmission slope decreases with I, creating curvature that cannot be matched by simply rescaling transmission_rate or other existing parent parameters.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Transmission is first-order in the infectious fraction, with no saturation or overlap on the infectious source side.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Transmission from infectious individuals has finite effective capacity, so source-side contribution saturates with I.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Taking infectious_saturation to infinity recovers the parent transmission law.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed S and B, the child predicts a concave-down transmission contribution as I increases, so trajectories that enter moderate-I regimes while S is still substantial show earlier slowdown and lower, broader peaks than the parent. This is a direct change in the scored target mapping dI_dt(S,I,B), not merely an auxiliary-state effect.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters preserves linear dependence of the transmission contribution on I at fixed S and B, so it cannot reproduce both near-low-I behavior and the stronger mid-I flattening across trajectories with different attained prevalence. Adjusting susceptible or burden-side parameters only rescales or shifts suppression through S and B, but does not create the required I-dependent curvature in the target equation.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when I reaches a non-negligible fraction of the population while S remains above the contact-limitation scale, so repeated contacts, local overlap, or finite effective mixing make added infectious individuals less than proportionally productive; weak when I stays very small throughout.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early-to-mid epidemic growth already shows slight downward bending of dI_dt versus I at moderate prevalence; in holdout, larger peaks extend this same mechanism into clearer sublinear transmission and stronger peak flattening without changing the sign structure.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the infectious-saturation scale to infinity, which restores exactly first-order transmission in I.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes every additional infectious individual contributes proportionally to new infections at all prevalence levels, after only susceptible-side and burden-side suppression are applied.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Transmission is first-order in the infectious fraction, with no saturation or overlap on the infectious source side.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: At moderate prevalence, infectious individuals increasingly compete for the same susceptible contacts or share overlapping contact neighborhoods, so total force of infection rises sublinearly with infectious abundance even in a closed homogeneous benchmark.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent’s exact mass-action dependence on I within the transmission term, not to add a wholly new biological process. The parent already includes susceptible limitation and burden-responsive suppression, but it still uses a single-phase linear infectiousness law: holding S, B, and parameters fixed, the transmission part of dI_dt scales exactly with I. Varying prevalence over trajectories while keeping the same parameter set and the same initial-condition contract, this implies one shared local slope of transmission with respect to I near low and moderate prevalence. In the child, the slope decreases as I grows because infectious contribution saturates, creating changed curvature in the scored target mapping dI_dt(S,I,B). This contrast is scientifically admissible when prevalence becomes moderate before susceptibles are exhausted; then overlap in contacted susceptibles or finite effective mixing reduces marginal transmission per extra infectious individual. The effect is not merely in an auxiliary state because it directly changes the target equation’s dependence on observed I. Limitation: if all observed trajectories remain in the very low-I regime, the refinement is weakly identifiable and the parent is approximately recovered.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

states.description: Lagged burden-response state tracking recent infectious burden

scenario_text: Model the rise and decline of an infectious population in a closed population where susceptible depletion is the main source of feedback. Susceptible and infectious fractions are jointly evolved from initial conditions, with infection generated by infectious contacts and infectious individuals removed at a constant rate. Recovered or otherwise removed individuals are not required as a dynamic state because they do not return to susceptibility in the baseline model. The target is the time derivative of the infectious fraction.
